slides.title: Pricing in 2027 while churn rises
Key questions

claims.claim: Should Palisade raise prices at 2027 renewals while churn rises, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR 15% with retention above 100%?
evidence: Decision maker: CEO, with the leadership team, approving the 2027 pricing plan
Success criteria: ARR grows at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M; Net revenue retention stays above 100% overall; Each price move rests on evidence for that segment
Timing: Leadership meeting, December 2026
Out of scope: New plans, such as a low-cost SMB tier; Enterprise contracts before renewal; New-customer sales targets

Sub-questions: 1 Where is churn rising, and is price the cause? 2 Which customers will accept a higher price in 2027? 3 What does each option add to 2027 ARR, and does it pass the 15% growth and 100% retention tests? 4 What will bring SMB churn down? 5 How do we roll the plan out in 2027, and what tells us it is working?

slides.title: Executive summary

claims.claim: Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay: 12% for mid-market, enterprise up to its caps, and SMB only after a test
Rising churn comes from 2025 promotion customers reaching full price: they explain 91% of the SMB rise
evidence: SMB churn outside the promotion moved only from 2.0% to 2.1% a month

claims.claim: Mid-market has shown it will pay more and enterprise rarely leaves, but SMB pricing is unproven with Inkwell at $9
evidence: Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year

claims.claim: The CFO's 12% can add only $7.6M in 2027, and mid-market and enterprise rises alone clear the $98.9M target
evidence: Without any SMB rise, 2027 ARR still reaches about $99.03M

claims.claim: Activation is the lever on the promotion cohort's churn, but fixing it cuts SMB churn by up to a third, not half
evidence: Only 41% of promotion customers activated in month one, against 72% elsewhere

claims.claim: Approve in December, raise mid-market and enterprise from January, and decide SMB in July
evidence: A Q1 test of +8% on non-promotion SMB renewals gates the July decision

slides.title: Rising churn is a promotion problem
Churn is rising because promotion customers hit full price, not because our core customers reject our prices

claims.claim: Churn rose almost only in SMB: mid-market moved a little and enterprise not at all, and the board's churn figure cannot be rebuilt from the segment data
evidence: 1.1 pp rise in SMB monthly logo churn, H1 2025 to H1 2026

claims.claim: Inside SMB, the customers who joined through the half-price promotion explain nearly all of the rise; the rest of SMB churns as it did a year ago
evidence: 91% of the SMB churn rise comes from the promotion cohort

claims.claim: Price complaints rose among promotion leavers; other SMB leavers cite price at about the rate all SMB leavers did a year earlier
evidence: 18% of non-promotion SMB churners cite price, against 19% of all SMB churners in H1 2025

slides.title: 1a: Churn is rising almost only in SMB, where monthly logo churn climbed from 2.0% to 3.1% in a year

claims.claim: Churn is rising almost only in SMB, where monthly logo churn climbed from 2.0% to 3.1% in a year
evidence: Monthly logo churn H1 2025 / H1 2026: SMB 2.0% / 3.1%; Mid-market 0.6% / 0.8%; Enterprise 0.2% / 0.2%

claims.claim: SMB is where we lose customers
evidence: 94% of the customers we lost each month in H1 2026 were SMB customers
Mid-2026 customer counts: 5,900 SMB, 1,350 mid-market, 150 enterprise

claims.claim: SMB: up by more than half in a year, across self-serve monthly and annual plans
Mid-market: a small rise from a low base; worth watching, not yet a trend
Enterprise: unchanged, on mostly multi-year contracts

slides.title: 1a: The board's 1.4% to 2.3% churn figure matches no measure we can rebuild and needs a definition

claims.claim: The board's 1.4% to 2.3% churn figure matches no measure we can rebuild and needs a definition
evidence: Board dashboard, Q2 2026: 1.4% to 2.3%; Not defined on the dashboard; periods not stated; Define it first / Agree one churn measure before the board judges the price plan
Customer-weighted logo churn: 1.7% to 2.6%; Best read of how many customers leave
ARR-weighted logo churn: 0.8% to 1.2%; Best read of how much revenue is exposed

slides.title: 1b: Outside the promotion cohort, SMB churn barely moved, from 2.0% to 2.1% a month

claims.claim: Outside the promotion cohort, SMB churn barely moved, from 2.0% to 2.1% a month
evidence: All SMB H1 2025 2.0%; All SMB H1 2026 3.1%; Non-promotion SMB H1 2025 2.0%; Non-promotion SMB H1 2026 2.1%; Promotion cohort H1 2026 4.9%

claims.claim: The promotion cohort is the rise
evidence: 91% of the SMB churn rise comes from the promotion cohort
Rest of SMB: had all SMB churned at its rate, churn would have risen 0.1 percentage points
Promotion-cohort rate implied as (3.1% × 5,900 − 2.1% × 3,800) ÷ 2,100

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: loses customers more than twice as fast as the rest of SMB
Timing: most promotion leavers went within two months of the discount ending

slides.title: 1b: The promotion cohort is 36% of SMB customers but more than half of the SMB customers we lose each month

claims.claim: The promotion cohort is 36% of SMB customers but more than half of the SMB customers we lose each month
evidence: 36% share of SMB customers (2,100 of 5,900, mid-2026)
56% share of SMB customers lost a month (from churn rates, H1 2026; about 103 of the 183 SMB customers lost a month)
47% share of SMB exit-survey answers (implied by the price-reason mix; the mix that makes 52% and 18% average to 34%)

claims.claim: Two separate reads put the cohort at about half or more of SMB churn
evidence: Churn rates: the cohort's implied rate gives the higher share
Exit survey: the price-reason mix gives a lower share, since not every leaver answers

claims.claim: Either way: SMB is shedding customers it bought at half price, not its core base
evidence: Joined Feb–Aug 2025 at 50% off for six months
About $4.4M of ARR at full price

slides.title: 1c: Promotion leavers drove the rise in price complaints; other SMB leavers cite price at about the old rate

claims.claim: Promotion leavers drove the rise in price complaints; other SMB leavers cite price at about the old rate
evidence: Share citing price: All SMB churners H1 2025 19%; All SMB churners H1 2026 34%; Promotion-cohort churners H1 2026 52%; Non-promotion SMB churners H1 2026 18%

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: most left within two months of the 50% discount ending, when they first paid full price
Non-promotion SMB: at the old all-SMB rate, even after Inkwell's $9 plan launched in October 2025
All SMB: the blended rise is a mix effect of more promotion leavers
Price is a churn risk where customers never got value from the product, not across the core base

slides.title: Rising churn is a promotion problem
Mid-market has shown it will pay more and enterprise rarely leaves; SMB pricing power is unproven

claims.claim: 2a: Mid-market buyers — room for 12% at renewal
evidence: A 10% higher list price left conversion at 23.1% against 23.6%
Tested at 10% on new sign-ups, not on renewals
12% at renewal; 85% of its ARR renews in 2027

claims.claim: 2b: Enterprise contracts — 7% where capped, 12% on the $3.8M uncapped
evidence: 118% net retention and 0.2% monthly churn; no price test yet
60% of ARR capped at 7% a year; 40% renews in 2027

claims.claim: 2c: SMB, 2023 precedent — Test before any rise; decide in July
evidence: The 2023 rise of 8% lifted churn for only six months
Made before Inkwell's $9 plan existed

claims.claim: 2d: Inkwell's reach — Pressure sits mostly in SMB
evidence: Not seen in mid-market or enterprise deals above 200 seats
Our SMB win rate against it fell from 51% to 38%

slides.title: 2a: A 10% higher mid-market list price left conversion statistically unchanged, our clearest sign of pricing power

claims.claim: A 10% higher mid-market list price left conversion statistically unchanged, our clearest sign of pricing power
evidence: 10% higher list price tested in 2024, against the 12% we propose
23.1% conversion of new sign-ups at the higher price, against 23.6% for the control group, 2024; Gap not statistically significant; Three-month test, new sign-ups
112% mid-market net revenue retention, against 94% in SMB
85% of mid-market ARR renews in 2027: $34.9M of its $41.0M ARR

claims.claim: Take 12% at renewal, a step past the tested 10%, and treat Q1 renewals as the check
evidence: The test measured new sign-ups; how renewing customers react is the open question, read out after Q1 2027

slides.title: 2b: Enterprise loyalty is high, but contracts leave little 2027 room: only $3.8M of its ARR renews without a cap

claims.claim: Enterprise loyalty is high, but contracts leave little 2027 room: only $3.8M of its ARR renews without a cap
evidence: Enterprise ARR: Not renewing in 2027 $14.4M; Renewing, capped at 7% $5.76M; Renewing, uncapped $3.84M
$9.6M enterprise ARR renewing in 2027 (40% of $24.0M) × 60% capped = $5.8M renewing under a cap

claims.claim: Valued, but locked in
evidence: Capped: those contracts can rise 7% a year, 5 percentage points short of the CFO's 12%
Loyalty: 118% net retention; integrations and the audit trail keep them

slides.title: 2c: The 2023 SMB price rise lifted churn for only six months before it settled near its old level

claims.claim: The 2023 SMB price rise lifted churn for only six months before it settled near its old level
evidence: SMB monthly churn: Before the rise 1.8%; First six months after 2.3%; Settled level 1.9%
Spike: churn ran 0.5 percentage points higher for six months
Settled: it ended 0.1 percentage points above where it started

claims.claim: Then and now: in 2023 no rival sold a $9 plan; today Inkwell does, so the same rise could cost more
Treat 2023 as the floor for SMB risk, not the forecast, and test before any SMB rise

slides.title: 2d: Inkwell pressures SMB prices: its Starter plan undercuts ours by 40%, and our win rate against it fell to 38%

claims.claim: Inkwell's $9 Starter plan sits 40% below our SMB plan
evidence: List price $/user/month: Palisade Business 29; Inkwell Pro 24; Palisade SMB 15; Inkwell Starter 9
A 12% SMB rise would take our SMB plan from $15 to $16.80 a user a month against Inkwell's $9

claims.claim: Our SMB win rate where Inkwell was considered fell 13 percentage points in a year
Inkwell is absent from deals above 200 seats, so its pressure sits mostly in SMB
evidence: Mid-market starts at 51 employees, so some mid-market accounts sit below 200 seats

slides.title: Rising churn is a promotion problem
Raising mid-market and enterprise alone clears the growth target, so SMB can wait for a test

claims.claim: The CFO's $10.3M cannot land in 2027: most enterprise ARR renews later and caps limit the rest
evidence: $7.6M of ARR a 12% rise on every plan can add in 2027

claims.claim: SMB is a third of that gain and carries most of the risk; it pays only if churn reacts less than three times as strongly as in 2023
evidence: 33% of the 12% plan's reachable gain comes from SMB

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise at the CFO's 12% (7% where capped) clear the target on their own; SMB follows a test
evidence: $99.03M 2027 ARR without any SMB rise, against a $98.9M target
Floor of the recommended plan: $93.98M today's customers at 2026 net retention + $5.05M mid-market and enterprise rise = $99.03M

slides.title: 3a: Only $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can land in 2027, because most enterprise ARR does not renew until later

claims.claim: Only $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can land in 2027, because most enterprise ARR does not renew until later
evidence: CFO plan: 12% of all ARR 10.32; Mid-market not renewing −0.74; Enterprise not renewing −1.73; Enterprise 7% caps −0.29; Reachable in 2027 7.57
27% of the CFO's figure cannot land in 2027

claims.claim: The $10.3M treats all ARR as renewing in 2027
evidence: Enterprise not renewing: 60% of its ARR is on multi-year terms that renew after 2027
Caps: renewing capped contracts can rise 7%, not 12%
Mid-market: 15% of its ARR renews after 2027
Before churn: no customer is assumed to leave because of the rise

slides.title: 3b: SMB brings a third of the CFO plan's gain, and it breaks even at three times the 2023 churn reaction

claims.claim: SMB brings a third of the CFO plan's gain, and it breaks even at three times the 2023 churn reaction
evidence: $2.5M SMB gain from 12% on $21.0M ARR ÷ $23.5M SMB ARR at the new price = 10.7% of SMB customers the rise could lose before it stops paying
10.7% ÷ 3.6% extra SMB customers lost in the first year after the 2023 rise = 3x

claims.claim: On 2023 behaviour the SMB rise pays; Inkwell is the open question
evidence: At the 2023 reaction the 12% rise loses about $0.85M of SMB ARR and nets about $1.67M
The 2023 reaction followed an 8% rise with no $9 competitor in the market
52% of promotion-cohort churners already cite price, and the cohort holds $4.4M of SMB ARR

slides.title: 3c: Retention plus 12% on mid-market and enterprise clears the growth target, with SMB adding only $0.34M after a test

claims.claim: The target does not depend on SMB
evidence: 2027 starting ARR 86; Net retention at 2026 rates +7.98; Mid-market and enterprise rise +5.05; SMB after the test, net +0.34; 2027 ARR before new customers 99.37
$0.5M above the $98.9M target (15% growth)

claims.claim: Net retention: the largest step; keeping mid-market and enterprise customers matters more than any price
evidence: Each percentage point of net retention moves 2027 ARR by $0.86M

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise: enough on their own; without any SMB rise ARR still reaches $99.03M
SMB: small once charged the 2023 churn reaction; its value is the evidence, not the money

slides.title: 3c: Mid-market carries the plan: $4.19M of the $5.39M it adds comes from mid-market renewals at 12%

claims.claim: Mid-market carries the plan: $4.19M of the $5.39M it adds comes from mid-market renewals at 12%
evidence: $4.2M mid-market: 12% on the $34.9M renewing in 2027
+ $0.9M enterprise: 7% on capped and 12% on uncapped renewals
+ $0.7M SMB: 8% on non-promotion renewals from July, only if the test passes
− $0.3M SMB ARR lost at the 2023 churn reaction
= $5.4M ARR added by the price plan in 2027
Non-promotion SMB ARR is $16.6M

claims.claim: Four assumptions for leadership to confirm in December
evidence: No extra mid-market or enterprise churn at 12%
Enterprise caps cover the same 60% share of the ARR renewing in 2027
SMB renewals spread evenly, so half fall after July; the promotion cohort gets no rise
The SMB rise carries the same 2023 churn charge as the CFO plan's SMB rise

slides.title: 3c: Of the three options, only holding SMB until a test meets the growth target whatever SMB customers do

claims.claim: Of the three options, only holding SMB until a test meets the growth target whatever SMB customers do
evidence: 12% on every plan (CFO): About $100.7M if SMB reacts as in 2023; misses if it reacts about three times as strongly
12% mid-market and enterprise, SMB after a test: About $99.4M; at least $99.03M whatever SMB customers do
Hold all prices: About $94.0M, $4.92M short unless new customers fill the gap
Estimated 2027 net revenue retention: about 117% (CFO plan), 116% (recommended), 109% (hold)

claims.claim: The CFO plan adds about $1.33M more only if SMB reacts as it did before Inkwell

slides.title: Rising churn is a promotion problem
Getting promotion customers to use the product is the fix for SMB churn, though it cannot halve it

claims.claim: 4a: Fixing the promotion cohort cuts SMB churn by up to a third, not half
evidence: 32% largest possible cut in SMB churn
Halving would take SMB churn below its level before the promotion
The core base already churns at 2.1% a month

claims.claim: 4b: Most of the cohort never got going, so activation is the lever
evidence: 41% of promotion customers activated, against 72% elsewhere
Low senders churn about three times as fast as the rest
Up to $1.48M of ARR a year rides on closing the gap

claims.claim: Target: SMB churn back to 2.1% a month; Owner: Head of Customer Success, from Q1 2027

slides.title: 4a: Halving SMB churn would go below any level in our data; fixing the promotion cohort cuts it a third at most

claims.claim: Halving SMB churn would go below any level in our data; fixing the promotion cohort cuts it a third at most
evidence: SMB today H1 2026 3.1%; Fully fixed promotion cohort 2.1%; SMB a year earlier H1 2025 2.0%; Customer Success claim 1.55%
32% largest cut from fixing the promotion cohort
Customer Success view: "An onboarding programme will halve SMB churn within two quarters"

claims.claim: The claim: halving would put SMB below its level before the promotion, which nothing in the data supports
Timing: the cohort's heaviest exits came right after the discount ended, and those customers have gone

slides.title: 4b: Most promotion customers never got going: 41% sent five documents in month one, against 72% elsewhere

claims.claim: Most promotion customers never got going: 41% sent five documents in month one, against 72% elsewhere
evidence: 41% of promotion customers sent five or more documents in their first month
72% of other SMB cohorts sent five or more documents in month one
Customer Success: they "never set the product up"

claims.claim: Month-one use predicts who stays
evidence: 3x the churn rate for SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in month one, compared with those who send more

claims.claim: The highest-risk group in the base
evidence: 4.9% implied monthly churn of the promotion cohort, H1 2026, more than twice the 2.1% of other SMB customers
52% of its leavers name price as the main reason

slides.title: 4b: Bringing the cohort's churn down to the rest of SMB would protect up to $1.48M of ARR a year

claims.claim: Bringing the cohort's churn down to the rest of SMB would protect up to $1.48M of ARR a year
evidence: $4.4M promotion-cohort ARR at full price, mid-2026 × 33.6% of cohort ARR lost a year beyond the rest of SMB (2.8 percentage points a month, 4.9% against 2.1%, for 12 months) = $1.5M of ARR a year at stake, an upper bound

claims.claim: An upper bound that sets the onboarding budget
evidence: The programme is worth running only if it costs well below this ceiling

slides.title: Rising churn is a promotion problem
The plan starts with mid-market and enterprise renewals in January and decides SMB pricing in July on test results

claims.claim: The plan starts with mid-market and enterprise renewals in January and decides SMB pricing in July on test results
evidence: Dec 2026: Plan approved; SMB decision, July
Churn measure: One definition; Segment and cohort churn reported monthly
Mid-market and enterprise: Mid-market +12%, enterprise 7% capped or 12%, at each renewal
SMB price: Test +8% on non-promotion renewals; Roll out only if the test passes
Promotion cohort: Onboarding to five documents in month one; Price held through 2027

claims.claim: If the SMB test fails, 2027 ARR still clears the target at about $99.03M

slides.title: 5a: A controlled test settles the open SMB price question before anyone outside it pays more

claims.claim: Prove that non-promotion SMB customers accept +8% before rolling it out
evidence: Non-promotion SMB ARR the test decides on: $16.6M
Design: Random half of non-promotion SMB renewals in Q1 at +8%, the rest at today's price; Promotion cohort left out of the test; Exit survey for every churned customer
Run: Monthly churn of the test and control groups; Share of leavers citing price, 18% today; Win rate against Inkwell, 38% today
Decide: Roll out in July if test churn stays within 0.5 percentage points of control, the 2023 spike; Otherwise hold SMB prices and rely on onboarding
Owner CFO, with the Head of Customer Success · Timing Jan–Jul 2027

slides.title: 5b: Onboarding for the promotion cohort aims at five documents in month one, the signal of who stays

claims.claim: Lift the promotion cohort from 41% activation toward the 72% of other cohorts
evidence: Cohort ARR at full price the programme protects: $4.4M
Reach: Contact all 2,100 promotion customers in Q1; Start with those below five documents sent so far
Activate: Guided setup of the first workflow and templates; Show the integrations and audit trail larger customers stay for
Measure: Cohort churn against 2.1% for the rest of SMB; Price held at today's level through 2027; Go or stop at the Q2 review
Owner Head of Customer Success · Timing Jan–Jun 2027

evidence: Renewing customers push back more than new sign-ups did; Early signal: Monthly churn above 0.8%; Response: Fall back to 10% for later renewal batches; Owner: Head of Sales; $4.19M of the 2027 price gain depends on it

claims.claim: Inkwell moves up-market
evidence: Inkwell appears in deals above 200 seats; Early signal: Any lost mid-market deal citing Inkwell; Response: Lead on integrations and the audit trail; Owner: CEO

claims.claim: SMB test fails
evidence: Test churn rises above control; Gap over 0.5 pp; Hold SMB prices; target still met; Owner: CFO; Decide in July

evidence: Mid-market monthly churn: 0.8%; Stays at or below today's level; Review the rise before the next renewal batch

slides.title: BACKUP: The promotion cohort's churn is implied from the blended SMB rate and the rate of the rest of SMB

evidence: 182.9 SMB customers lost a month (3.1% of 5,900) − 79.8 non-promotion customers lost a month (2.1% of 3,800) = 103.1 promotion-cohort customers lost a month
103.1 ÷ 2,100 promotion customers = 4.9% implied monthly churn

claims.claim: An approximation that the exit survey cross-checks
evidence: Mid-2026 customer counts stand in for the average H1 2026 base
The exit-survey mix gives a lower 47% promotion share of leavers, against 56% here
Promotion customers who left before mid-2026 are not in the base and not counted

slides.title: BACKUP: Three churn measures answer different questions, and the board dashboard should name the one it shows

claims.claim: Three churn measures answer different questions, and the board dashboard should name the one it shows
evidence: Customer-weighted logo churn: Customers lost in the month ÷ customers at the start of the month; dominated by SMB, which has 80% of customers
ARR-weighted logo churn: Each segment's logo churn weighted by its share of ARR
Net revenue retention: ARR today from customers of 12 months ago ÷ their ARR then
Board dashboard figure: Not defined; matches neither weighting above; Replace with the measures above, by segment and for the promotion cohort

slides.title: BACKUP: Each piece of pricing evidence answers part of the question, and the gaps set what we test in 2027

claims.claim: Each piece of pricing evidence answers part of the question, and the gaps set what we test in 2027
evidence: 2024 mid-market test: New sign-ups accepted a 10% higher list price; cannot show how renewing customers react, or to 12%; Supports 12% at renewal; Q1 renewals watched
2023 SMB rise: A temporary churn spike after an 8% rise; cannot show the reaction with a $9 rival in the market; Sets the 8% test rate and the 0.5 pp gate
Exit survey: Why leavers say they left, by group; cannot show reasons of leavers who did not answer
Inkwell win rate: Lost SMB deals where Inkwell was considered; cannot show whether existing customers will switch; Guardrail on SMB list price
Customer advisory board: Why larger customers stay; cannot show how much more they would pay; Supports the mid-market and enterprise rise

slides.title: BACKUP: The 2027 ARR estimate rests on seven inputs for leadership to confirm

evidence: Net revenue retention held for 2027: 109.3%; ARR-weighted trailing rate by segment
Mid-market and uncapped enterprise rise: 12%; The CFO's rate; the 2024 test at 10% is the nearest evidence
Mid-market ARR renewing in 2027: 85%; Contract calendar, as briefed
Enterprise rise, capped contracts: 7%; Contract cap
SMB rise, non-promotion customers: 8%; The 2023 rise, the only one with a known reaction
SMB churn charge, first year: 3.6%; The 2023 reaction: 0.5 pp for six months, then 0.1 pp
Share of SMB renewals after July: 50%; Chosen for this deck: renewals spread evenly
The 2027 starting base is the $86.0M of mid-2026 ARR, as in the 15% target

slides.title: BACKUP: The plan clears the target unless mid-market renewals or net retention slip, the two risks to watch first

evidence: Recommended plan: $99.4M; Base case
SMB test fails, SMB prices held: $99.03M; still above target
Net retention 1 percentage point lower: $98.5M; Each point is worth $0.86M; below target

evidence: Renewal calendar by month: Sets how much of the rise lands in 2027; Billing system; CFO

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay: 12% for mid-market, enterprise up to its caps (7% capped, 12% uncapped), and SMB only after a test. Approve in December, raise mid-market and enterprise from January, and decide SMB in July, gated by a Q1 test of +8% on non-promotion SMB renewals; hold the promotion cohort's price through 2027 and run onboarding to five documents in month one; agree one churn definition for the board dashboard.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: only $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can land in 2027; about $100.7M if SMB reacts as in 2023 but misses if it reacts about three times as strongly; 'The CFO plan adds about $1.33M more only if SMB reacts as it did before Inkwell'.

alternatives_considered.option: 12% mid-market and enterprise (7% where capped), SMB after a test

alternatives_considered.treatment: Left out: outside our influence; enterprise contracts follow their own terms.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data: the company and all figures are fictional
Estimates hold 2026 net revenue retention (109.3%) for 2027 and count no new-customer ARR
No extra mid-market or enterprise churn at 12%; the 2024 test covered new sign-ups at 10%, so Q1 renewals are the check
Enterprise caps cover the same 60% share of the ARR renewing in 2027
SMB renewals spread evenly, so half fall after July; the promotion cohort gets no rise
The SMB rise carries the same 2023 churn charge (3.6% first year) as the CFO plan's SMB rise
SMB rate of 8% repeats the 2023 rise, the only SMB rise with a known reaction; plan parameters chosen for this deck, to confirm in December
Treat 2023 as the floor for SMB risk, not the forecast; in 2023 no rival sold a $9 plan, so the same rise could cost more

Promotion-cohort churn (4.9%) is implied; mid-2026 customer counts stand in for the H1 2026 base; promotion customers who left before mid-2026 are not counted; exit survey gives a lower 47% share against 56%
Not every churner answers the exit survey
The board's 1.4% to 2.3% churn figure is not defined and matches no rebuilt measure
Mid-market 2024 test measured new sign-ups; how renewing customers react is the open question, read out after Q1 2027
Mid-market starts at 51 employees, so some mid-market accounts sit below 200 seats and may meet Inkwell
Break-even: lost customers are valued at the new price for a full year; effects on new SMB sales are not counted
$1.48M ARR at stake is an upper bound; no compounding; no price rise on the cohort in 2027
Before churn: no customer is assumed to leave because of the rise (3a calculation)
Sensitivities: net retention 1 point lower gives $98.5M (below target); mid-market renewals reacting as SMB did in 2023 gives $97.96M (below target)
Risks: mid-market renewal reaction ($4.19M depends on it), Inkwell moves up-market, SMB test fails, promotion cohort leaves anyway
Data gaps: renewal calendar by month, mid-market seat mix, SMB plan mix, 2027 new-customer bookings, onboarding cost
